text: ARES requires a human preference validation set of approximately 150 to 300 annotated datapoints to compute confidence intervals for its prediction-powered inference [S4][S5][S6]. In contrast, RAGAS uses GPT-3.5 as its judge with few-shot prompts that are not targeted for each evaluation domain, and the sources do not specify a requirement for human annotations for RAGAS [S1][S3]. ARES is described as being significantly more data-efficient with human annotations compared to standard sampled annotation methods [S2].
